detail.body:
**Merge hold: keep this PR unmerged for investigation of the reproduced small-batch device cost.** The many-sequence improvement does not cancel this regression.

Packed context-parallel attention can spend substantial time locating each THD work item: the forward kernel scans every sequence and repeats head/tile division at every visit. This change stops at the owning sequence and computes those coordinates once. When the first and last entries of the existing longest-first GPU remap have the same rounded tile count, it locates the owning sequence directly. This also supports unequal sequence lengths within one tile bucket.

The optimization reads current device metadata on every execution, preserving ragged layouts, empty sequences, scheduler order and attention arithmetic. Initial admission is limited to SM100-family D128 BF16, top-left causal THD, 128×128 tiles, two CTAs and SPLIT_KV=1. The same opt-in also reaches paged THD through the shared D128 body, including eligible SM107 paged plans. Work ownership is determined by packed Q tiles; Q and KV lengths need not match. Other helper consumers retain their existing decoder. No public API, engine capability or heuristic changes are introduced.

Validation on a production B200 (148 SMs), cuDNN 9.27, CuTeDSL 4.8 with the CUDA 13 compiler flavor, and a freshly built FE native binding:

- 75 tests passed, zero failures or skips: 36 new cases and 39 existing THD cases.
- New cases cover three MHA/GQA head configurations, packing on/off, all three schedulers, both packed-LSE layouts, changing lengths/remap/input values on one CUDA Graph, all-empty work followed by live work, untouched output tails, and independent CPU FP64 O/LSE references.
- One representative case is collected by default L0; the complete new matrix is selected with `-m 'L0 or L1'`.
- Repository format and SPDX hooks passed.
- Compute Sanitizer 13.2 memcheck: the representative L0 graph-replay case passed with zero errors using explicit CUDA API error reporting and memory instrumentation enabled. Default extended reporting initially counted a Torch random-input code-recompilation warning; that first run is not treated as a zero-error pass.

Follow-up paged coverage: all 42 tests in this file passed on B200 (36 existing plus 6 new paged combinations), with zero skips. The new BF16 top-left causal cases cover NHD/HND pools, GQA ratio 6 with partial PackGQA, unequal Q/KV lengths, separate changing K/V page tables, all three schedulers, both packed-LSE layouts, empty-to-live replay, tail canaries, and an independent CPU FP64 O/LSE reference. They assert both the paged route and the bounded decoder. The two default-L0 paged cases also passed Compute Sanitizer memcheck with zero errors, explicit CUDA API error reporting, and memory instrumentation enabled. This follow-up changes tests and scope comments only; it does not change runtime admission or attention arithmetic. The controlled B200 experiment below reproduces a small-batch device-latency increase. Correctness passes do not clear that performance hold.

Run the new coverage from `test/python`:

```bash
pytest sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_thd_work_lookup.py -m 'L0 or L1'
```

Paired local forward measurements on B200 (148 SMs, default 1000W), BF16 top-left causal native THD, Hq/Hkv=8/2, D128, 524288 total tokens, including packed FP32 LSE and metadata helpers:

| Batch × sequence | Parent (ms) | This PR (ms) | Paired latency change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256 × 2K | 6.176 | 2.189 | -64.57% |
| 128 × 4K | 5.554 | 3.924 | -29.34% |
| 16 × 32K | 28.097 | 28.065 | +0.05% |

Both arms use parent `2bcdd1bb`, the same freshly built FE native binding and identical knobs (128×128, two CTAs, packed GQA, LPT, no split). The control retains the exact parent decoder; the candidate is the submitted source. Each shape uses a fresh process, warm plans, four balanced arm orders and three CUDA-event timing blocks per arm/order. Three shapes passed 264 O/LSE comparisons and 144 validated timing windows. The large-batch short-sequence gains reproduce; the 32K difference is effectively flat and is not claimed as a gain.

## Small-batch regression follow-up

A separate controlled experiment on one production B200 (148 SMs, default 1000 W, exclusive allocation) compares the retained original decoder with the bounded decoder inside current-head source. Both arms use BF16 top-left causal packed THD, Hq/Hkv=8/2, D128, 128x128 tiles, two CTAs, PackGQA, LPT and no split. The timed public FE graph includes forward, packed FP32 LSE and metadata helpers.

| Batch x sequence | Original decoder, eager GPU interval | Bounded decoder, eager GPU interval | Median paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 x 2048 | 34.192 us | 34.616 us | **+1.25%** |
| 64 x 512 | 140.759 us | 69.780 us | -50.42% |

Each shape uses four fresh processes with reversed construction orders. Every process builds two independent original-decoder and two independent bounded-decoder CUDA functions, with both FE cache layers disabled. All arms share input/output/workspace addresses within that process. Eight balanced timing rounds per process retain A/A controls as well as A/B comparisons. All 864 complete CPU-FP64 O/LSE validation stages pass, including poisoned replay and changed input values.

The single-sequence eager interval increases in all four processes (1.216-1.253%); its independent-compilation A/A envelope is 0.147%. Graph replay also increases, with a +3.55% paired median and a wider 3.48% A/A envelope, so the stable eager result is the primary hold evidence. The many-sequence replay change is -49.62%. Host submission has no established repeatable regression, but remains inconclusive under the predeclared criterion rather than being certified unchanged. Workspace size is equal; shared-buffer process memory is stable.

Only the eight expected worker processes appear in GPU telemetry. All sampled measurement-window clocks are 1965 MHz without clock-event flags; clocks were unlocked and 1 Hz sampling cannot resolve every timing phase. This is a local decoder experiment, not a full-base integration comparison, an isolated-main-kernel attribution, a TE CP result or an FA4 comparison. Keep the PR open for human analysis of the small-batch cost.

These are local forward-plus-LSE measurements. This PR does not claim full context-parallel end-to-end improvement; TE forward integration, backward and communication measurements remain separate work.




<!-- te-cp-lookup-followup-20261019 -->
### Follow-up regression result: hold retained

A private follow-up candidate on the current integration stack preserves the original B=1 decoder and applies the bounded lookup only to multi-batch inputs. It is **not published in this PR head**. The complete prospective study on an exclusive production B200 (148 SMs, default 1000 W; cuDNN 9.27, CUDA 13.2 and CuTeDSL 4.8 CUDA 13 flavor) uses BF16 causal THD, Hq8/Hkv2/D128, four fresh processes per shape, and independent AA/BB controls.

All **1,152 full O/LSE checks pass**, with no observed allocation growth during timing. B=1 passes all four bounded host/eager/replay metrics. The follow-up nevertheless has **small-batch device regressions**:

| Shape | Full-chain eager wall baseline / candidate | Paired change |
|---|---:|---:|
| B1/S2048 | 33.734 / 33.727 us | -0.003% |
| B2/S512 | 15.851 / 16.413 us | +3.492% |
| B5/S513 | 18.356 / 18.643 us | +1.534% |
| B64/S512 | 140.462 / 70.508 us | -49.800% |

The B2/B5 eager regressions have sufficiently precise AA/BB controls. Across all shapes and host submission, eager stream, eager wall and complete graph replay, **5 metrics pass, 5 remain inconclusive, and 6 trigger regression holds**. B64's observed gain does not clear the remaining control-precision gates or offset regressions elsewhere. These are FE component measurements, not TE/CP end-to-end results or benchmark-grid wins.

The private candidate is not promoted and the prepared full-CP comparison is not admitted. The completed experiment and all original holds are retained. A narrower lookup policy must receive independent correctness, sanitizer, excluded-shape and prospective host/device performance checks before reconsidering promotion. This PR remains on hold; no runtime source was changed by this update.
<!-- /te-cp-lookup-followup-20261019 -->

+        u = linear_cta // cutlass.Int32(CFG.CGA_M)

+        if cutlass.const_expr(getattr(CFG, "SPLIT_KV", 1) > 1):

+        # makes every downstream consumer a no-op through IN-BOUNDS metadata

+        # KV range in every role), the epilogue's per-sequence Q length
+        # cu[2n+1]-cu[2n] goes negative (LSE predicate never fires), and the
+        # O-store role skips the TMA store explicitly (batch >= n_batch).
+        f_batch = n_batch
+        f_head = cutlass.Int32(0)
+        f_qc = cutlass.Int32(0)
+        found_cb = cutlass.Int32(1)
+        found_local = cutlass.Int32(0)
+        done = cutlass.Int32(0)
+        remap0 = cutlass.Int32(3) * n_batch + cutlass.Int32(2)
+        search = cutlass.Int32(1)
+        # batch_remap is sorted by decreasing Q length. Rounding length to
+        # tile count is monotone, so equal endpoint counts prove that EVERY
+        # batch has the same count, including unequal lengths in one bucket.
+        # All observations are current device metadata; no host promise.
+        if n_batch > cutlass.Int32(0):
+            first_b = cutlass.Int32(cu[remap0])
+            last_b = cutlass.Int32(cu[remap0 + n_batch - cutlass.Int32(1)])
+            first_s = cutlass.Int32(cu[cuq0 + first_b + cutlass.Int32(1)]) - cutlass.Int32(cu[cuq0 + first_b])
+            last_s = cutlass.Int32(cu[cuq0 + last_b + cutlass.Int32(1)]) - cutlass.Int32(cu[cuq0 + last_b])
+            first_cb = (first_s + cutlass.Int32(thd_token_tile_m - 1)) // cutlass.Int32(thd_token_tile_m)
+            last_cb = (last_s + cutlass.Int32(thd_token_tile_m - 1)) // cutlass.Int32(thd_token_tile_m)
+            if first_cb == last_cb:
+                search = cutlass.Int32(0)
+                if first_cb > cutlass.Int32(0):
+                    per_batch = first_cb * n_qh
+                    ordinal = u // per_batch

+                        found_cb = first_cb
+                        found_local = u % per_batch
+                        done = cutlass.Int32(1)
+        i = cutlass.Int32(0)
+        # Preserve longest-first remapping and the DEAD-unit sentinel. Empty
+        # batches consume zero work. No host knowledge of lengths is needed.
+        while (i < n_batch) & (done == cutlass.Int32(0)) & (search != cutlass.Int32(0)):
+            b = cutlass.Int32(cu[remap0 + i])
+            s_i = cutlass.Int32(cu[cuq0 + b + cutlass.Int32(1)]) - cutlass.Int32(cu[cuq0 + b])

+            i = i + cutlass.Int32(1)

+        if done != cutlass.Int32(0):

+            f_qc = found_local % found_cb

+                    f_head = (found_local // (found_cb * group)) * group + found_local % group
+                    f_qc = found_cb - cutlass.Int32(1) - (found_local // group) % found_cb
+        q_super = f_qc * cutlass.Int32(_q_supers_per_cluster) + cta_in_pair
+        return q_super, f_head, f_batch + split * n_batch

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+
+"""THD work lookup across changing ragged metadata on a retained CUDA graph."""
+
+import itertools
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from test_utils import torch_fork_set_rng
+from frost_test_utils import requires_dsl
+
+
+def _build_graph(q, k, v, cu, max_seqlen, stats_layout, pack, policy, monkeypatch, *, page_tables=None, kv_lengths=None):
+    """Pin the bounded decoder with packed Q/O and either packed or paged K/V."""
+    import cudnn
+    import cudnn.sdpa.fwd.api_dsl as api_dsl
+
+    batch, hq, hkv, dim = cu.numel() - 1, q.shape[1], k.shape[1], q.shape[2]
+    capacity = q.shape[0]
+    io = cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16
+    g = cudnn.pygraph(io_data_type=io, intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT, compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT)
+    bindings, inputs, origins = {}, {}, []
+
+    def ragged_tensor(name, buf, heads):
+        tensor = g.tensor(name=name, dim=[batch, heads, max_seqlen, dim], stride=[max_seqlen * heads * dim, dim, heads * dim, 1], data_type=io)
+        offset = (cu.to(torch.int64) * heads * dim).view(batch + 1, 1, 1, 1)
+        ref = g.tensor_like(offset, name=name + "_origin")
+        tensor.set_ragged_offset(ref)
+        bindings.update({tensor: buf, ref: offset})
+        origins.append((offset, heads * dim))
+        return tensor
+
+    inputs["q"] = ragged_tensor("q", q, hq)
+    for name, buf in (("k", k), ("v", v)):
+        if page_tables is None:
+            inputs[name] = ragged_tensor(name, buf, hkv)
+        else:
+            inputs[name] = g.tensor_like(buf, name=name)
+            bindings[inputs[name]] = buf
+    cu4 = cu.view(batch + 1, 1, 1, 1)
+    sq = g.tensor_like(cu4, name="cu_q")
+    bindings[sq] = cu4
+    if page_tables is None:
+        sk = g.tensor_like(cu4, name="cu_kv")
+        bindings[sk] = cu4
+        kv_args = dict(cu_seq_len_kv=sk)
+    else:
+        sk = g.tensor_like(kv_lengths, name="seq_kv")
+        bindings[sk] = kv_lengths
+        tables = [g.tensor_like(buf, name=name) for name, buf in zip(("k_table", "v_table"), page_tables)]
+        bindings.update(zip(tables, page_tables))
+        kv_args = dict(
+            seq_len_kv=sk,
+            paged_attention_k_table=tables[0],
+            paged_attention_v_table=tables[1],
+            paged_attention_max_seq_len_kv=page_tables[0].shape[2] * k.shape[2],
+        )
+    o, stats = g.sdpa(
+        **inputs,
+        generate_stats=True,
+        attn_scale=dim**-0.5,
+        use_padding_mask=True,
+        use_causal_mask=True,
+        cu_seq_len_q=sq,
+        **kv_args,
+    )
+    ob = torch.empty_like(q)
+    token_major = stats_layout == "token"
+    sb = torch.empty((capacity, hq) if token_major else (hq, capacity), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for tensor, name, factor in ((o, "o_origin", hq * dim), (stats, "stats_origin", hq if token_major else 1)):
+        offset = (cu.to(torch.int64) * factor).view(batch + 1, 1, 1, 1)
+        ref = g.tensor_like(offset, name=name)
+        tensor.set_ragged_offset(ref)
+        origins.append((offset, factor))
+        bindings[ref] = offset
+    o.set_output(True).set_dim([batch, hq, max_seqlen, dim]).set_stride([max_seqlen * hq * dim, dim, hq * dim, 1])
+    stats.set_output(True).set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT).set_dim([batch, hq, max_seqlen, 1])
+    stats.set_stride([max_seqlen * hq, 1, hq, 1] if token_major else [max_seqlen * hq, capacity, 1, 1])
+    bindings.update({o: ob, stats: sb})
+    g.validate()
+    g.build_operation_graph()
+    g.create_execution_plans([cudnn.heur_mode.A])
+    names = [g.get_plan_name_at_index(i) for i in range(len(g.plans))]
+    arch = "sm107" if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (10, 7) else "sm100"
+    index = next((i for i, name in enumerate(names) if name.split("[")[0] == "sdpa_fwd_prefill_" + arch), None)
+    assert index is not None, names  # A missing FROST route must not silently skip this test.
+    engine, knobs = g.get_engine_and_knobs_at_index(index)
+    knobs.update(
+        {
+            cudnn.knob_type.PACK_GQA: pack,
+            cudnn.knob_type.SCHED_POLICY: policy,
+            cudnn.knob_type.TILE_M: 128,
+            cudnn.knob_type.TILE_N: 128,
+            cudnn.knob_type.TILE_CGA_M: 2,
+            cudnn.knob_type.SPLIT_KV: 1,
+        }
+    )
+    g.create_execution_plan(engine, knobs)
+    g.select_plan(len(g.plans) - 1)
+    loaded = []
+    load_module = api_dsl._load_sm100_kernel_module
+
+    def record_module(*args, **kwargs):
+        module = load_module(*args, **kwargs)
+        loaded.append(module)
+        return module
+
+    with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+        patch.setattr(api_dsl, "_load_sm100_kernel_module", record_module)
+        g.build_plans()
+    assert loaded and all(m._BOUNDED_THD_DECODE for m in loaded)
+    if page_tables is not None:
+        assert all(m.CFG.PAGED_KV for m in loaded), "The paged bounded decoder must be exercised"
+    workspace = torch.empty(max(1, g.get_workspace_size()), device=q.device, dtype=torch.uint8)
+
+    def execute():
+        g.execute(bindings, workspace)
+
+    def set_lengths(lengths):
+        cu.copy_(torch.tensor([0, *itertools.accumulate(lengths)], device=q.device, dtype=torch.int32))
+        for offset, factor in origins:
+            offset.copy_((cu.to(torch.int64) * factor).view(batch + 1, 1, 1, 1))
+
+    return execute, set_lengths, (ob, sb if token_major else sb.transpose(0, 1))
+
+
+def _reference(q, k, v, lengths):
+    """Independent CPU FP64 attention, including grouped heads and natural-log LSE."""
+    outputs, stats, start = [], [], 0
+    for length in lengths:
+        if length == 0:
+            continue
+        qq = q[start : start + length].cpu().double().transpose(0, 1)
+        kk, vv = (x[start : start + length].cpu().double().transpose(0, 1).repeat_interleave(q.shape[1] // k.shape[1], 0) for x in (k, v))
+        score = (qq @ kk.transpose(-1, -2)) * q.shape[2] ** -0.5
+        score.masked_fill_(torch.arange(length)[None, :] > torch.arange(length)[:, None], -torch.inf)
+        outputs.append((score.softmax(-1) @ vv).transpose(0, 1))
+        stats.append(score.logsumexp(-1).transpose(0, 1))
+        start += length
+    return torch.cat(outputs), torch.cat(stats)
+
+
+@requires_dsl
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "heads,pack,policy,stats_layout",
+    [
+        pytest.param(heads, pack, policy, layout, marks=pytest.mark.L0 if (heads, pack, policy, layout) == ((4, 1), 1, 1, "token") else pytest.mark.L1)
+        for heads, pack, policy, layout in itertools.product(((4, 1), (8, 8), (32, 8)), (0, 1), (0, 1, 2), ("token", "head"))
+    ],
+)
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=13)
+def test_thd_work_lookup_replay(heads, pack, policy, stats_layout, monkeypatch):
+    major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
+    if major != 10 or minor >= 7:
+        pytest.skip("SM100-family forward kernel")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FROST_THD_CLUSTERS", "4")
+    hq, hkv = heads
+    batch, max_seqlen, dim = 5, 2049, 128
+    q, k, v = (torch.randn(batch * max_seqlen, h, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.5 for h in (hq, hkv, hkv))
+    cu = torch.arange(batch + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32) * max_seqlen
+    execute, set_lengths, actual = _build_graph(q, k, v, cu, max_seqlen, stats_layout, pack, policy, monkeypatch)
+    # Force several persistent claims per cluster, including dead overlaunch.
+    for _ in range(3):
+        execute()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    try:
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            execute()
+        length_sets = [
+            [0, 1, 511, 1024, 513],
+            [768, 0, 3, 1025, 253],
+            [513, 560, 575, 520, 544],  # Unequal lengths, equal rounded tile counts.
+            [572, 515, 550, 565, 519],  # Different longest-first permutation.
+            [0, 0, 0, 0, 0],
+            [513, 560, 575, 520, 544],  # Live again without recapture.
+        ]
+        for iteration, lengths in enumerate(length_sets):
+            set_lengths(lengths)
+            v.mul_(-1)  # Replayed outputs cannot be inherited from an earlier iteration.
+            for buf in actual:
+                buf.fill_(float("nan"))
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            total = sum(lengths)
+            for buf in actual:
+                assert torch.isnan(buf[total:]).all(), (iteration, "dead rows were written")
+            if total:
+                reference = _reference(q, k, v, lengths)
+                for role, got, want in zip(("o", "stats"), actual, reference):
+                    tolerance = 0.01 if role == "o" else 1e-4
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(got[:total].cpu().double(), want, atol=tolerance, rtol=tolerance)
+        previous_mode = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+        try:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+            execute()
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous_mode)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    finally:
+        graph.reset()
+
+
+def _paged_reference(q, k, v, page_tables, q_lengths, kv_lengths):
+    """CPU FP64 top-left causal attention over independently gathered K/V pages."""
+    q, k, v = (buf.cpu().double() for buf in (q, k, v))
+    kt, vt = (table.cpu().view(len(q_lengths), -1).long() for table in page_tables)
+    hq, hkv, dim = q.shape[1], k.shape[1], q.shape[2]
+    out = torch.zeros(sum(q_lengths), hq, dim, dtype=torch.float64)
+    stats = torch.full((sum(q_lengths), hq), -torch.inf, dtype=torch.float64)
+    start = 0
+    for i, (nq, nk) in enumerate(zip(q_lengths, kv_lengths)):
+        if nq and nk:
+            kk, vv = (pool[table[i]].transpose(1, 2).reshape(-1, hkv, dim)[:nk].repeat_interleave(hq // hkv, 1) for pool, table in ((k, kt), (v, vt)))
+            qq = q[start : start + nq].transpose(0, 1)
+            score = (qq @ kk.transpose(0, 1).transpose(-1, -2)) * dim**-0.5
+            score.masked_fill_(torch.arange(nk)[None, :] > torch.arange(nq)[:, None], -torch.inf)
+            out[start : start + nq] = (score.softmax(-1) @ vv.transpose(0, 1)).transpose(0, 1)
+            stats[start : start + nq] = score.logsumexp(-1).transpose(0, 1)
+        start += nq
+    return out, stats
+
+
+@requires_dsl
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("hnd", [False, True], ids=["NHD", "HND"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "policy,stats_layout",
+    [
+        pytest.param(0, "token", marks=pytest.mark.L0),
+        pytest.param(1, "head", marks=pytest.mark.L1),
+        pytest.param(2, "token", marks=pytest.mark.L1),
+    ],
+)
+@torch_fork_set_rng(seed=17)
+def test_thd_work_lookup_paged_replay(hnd, policy, stats_layout, monkeypatch):
+    """BF16 causal paged THD with unequal Q/KV lengths and partial PackGQA."""
+    from test_sdpa_fwd_paged_sm100 import _pools
+
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3), (10, 7)):
+        pytest.skip("Shared paged D128 kernel on SM100, SM103 and SM107")
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (10, 7) and policy == 2:
+        pytest.skip("The SM107 graph row does not offer LPT_L2 for BF16")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("FROST_THD_CLUSTERS", "4")
+    batch, max_seqlen, hq, hkv, dim = 3, 513, 12, 2, 128
+    # Six query heads per KV head leave a partial group in the packing tile.
+    rng = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(17)
+    _, _, k, v, table = _pools(batch, hkv, dim, 16, 40, hnd, torch.bfloat16, generator=rng)
+    k.mul_(0.5)
+    v.mul_(0.5)
+    page_tables = (table, table.flip(2))
+    q = torch.randn(batch * max_seqlen, hq, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16, generator=rng) * 0.5
+    cu = torch.arange(batch + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32) * max_seqlen
+    kv_lengths = torch.full((batch, 1, 1, 1), 640, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    execute, set_lengths, actual = _build_graph(q, k, v, cu, max_seqlen, stats_layout, 1, policy, monkeypatch, page_tables=page_tables, kv_lengths=kv_lengths)
+    for _ in range(3):
+        execute()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    try:
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            execute()
+        for ql, kl in (
+            ([0, 129, 513], [640, 63, 257]),
+            ([257, 0, 1], [513, 0, 0]),
+            ([129, 140, 151], [211, 99, 640]),  # Equal rounded Q tile counts.
+            ([150, 130, 141], [79, 512, 199]),  # New longest-first remap.
+            ([0, 0, 0], [0, 640, 1]),
+            ([129, 140, 151], [211, 99, 640]),
+        ):
+            set_lengths(ql)
+            kv_lengths.copy_(torch.tensor(kl, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).view_as(kv_lengths))
+            q.mul_(-1)
+            v.mul_(-1)
+            for table in page_tables:
+                table.copy_(table.roll(1, dims=2))
+            for buf in actual:
+                buf.fill_(float("nan"))
+            graph.replay()
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            total = sum(ql)
+            for buf in actual:
+                assert torch.isnan(buf[total:]).all(), "Dead packed rows were written"
+            if total:
+                for role, got, want in zip(("o", "stats"), actual, _paged_reference(q, k, v, page_tables, ql, kl)):
+                    tolerance = 0.01 if role == "o" else 1e-4
+                    torch.testing.assert_close(got[:total].cpu().double(), want, atol=tolerance, rtol=tolerance)
+        previous_mode = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
+        try:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode("error")
+            execute()
+        finally:
+            torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous_mode)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    finally:
+        graph.reset()

Independent measurement also supports the intended large-batch, short-sequence benefit.
